response.markdown_report:
At 10% research progress, prioritize a controlled diagnostic extension before changing HSTU training. No measured results establish the proposed mechanism yet.

**Starting-point insights.** (1) Deleting events changes both content and occupied positions. Fixed-slot replacements can reduce this confounding. (2) Final-event removal changes the readout context. Preserving the final event makes earlier-history comparisons more interpretable. (3) User feedback suggests excessive historical affinity. This motivates a hypothesis about stale-history dependence, but does not establish ownership, satisfied needs, or intent.

**Related-work insights.** (1) HSTU combines aggregated attention, gating, and relative biases [1]. Input interventions can probe their combined behavior without assuming unavailable internal hooks. (2) Recency-bias research cautions that recent-history dependence can itself be excessive [2]. Both recent and older interventions therefore need measurement. (3) Sampled ranking can disagree with full-catalog ranking [3]. Diagnostic ranks must remain distinct from the pinned validation selection metric.

Three research directions follow: controlled history sensitivity, component attribution, and evidence-aware interpretation.

| Direction | Existing approach | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| History sensitivity | Deletion and shuffle | Content removal changes positions |
| Component attribution | Frozen gate/bias ablation | Hooks may be unavailable; interventions can shift activations |
| Interpretation | Functional relation annotation [4] | Titles cannot establish satisfied needs |

Three atomic ideas are feasible. Scores below are originality/potential/difficulty, with higher difficulty meaning harder implementation.

- **Matched fixed-slot replacement: 5/8/3.** Originality: strengthens existing controls, although replacement probes are established. Potential: directly tests the stale-history hypothesis, although synthetic inputs limit interpretation. Difficulty: uses existing scoring hooks, although matching requires care.
- **Frozen gate neutralization: 4/6/6.** Originality: targets HSTU structure, although ablation is standard. Potential: localizes sensitivity, although frozen ablations do not predict retraining benefits. Difficulty: small intervention once exposed, although internal hooks are unspecified.
- **Evidence-backed relation audit: 5/7/7.** Originality: connects functional relations to ranking errors, although annotation methods exist. Potential: clarifies user feedback, although sparse descriptions force abstention. Difficulty: needs little model code, although calibration requires human annotation.

Select **matched fixed-slot replacement**. For each eligible training prefix, preserve its target, final event, padding, occupied slots, and shared diagnostic candidates. Replace equal-sized recent and older nonfinal windows using the same replacement-item multiset, matched approximately on training frequency. Include identity and matched-random-window controls. Report paired target-rank, reciprocal-rank, and top-10 entry/exit effects, with user-cluster bootstrap intervals.

An improvement after replacing older events indicates harmful dependence under that intervention; it does not establish obsolete intent. Preserve the diagnostic adapter contracts and restore model modes and RNG states. Keep one HSTU checkpoint per category and use only the fixed four-category macro validation HR@10 for model selection.

References: [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17152; [2] https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722; [3] https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/; [4] https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html.

idea.description: Extend the existing HSTU diagnosis adapter with paired, fixed-slot replacements of recent versus older nonfinal history windows, using one frozen trained checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: Existing deletion probes confound removed content with position changes. User feedback motivates testing whether older history harms target ranking, while preserving the final readout event and avoiding unsupported claims about intent or satisfied needs.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Use view.model in evaluation/inference mode and preserve item_emb, log2feats(sequence), and predict_score(features, items). Select prefixes exclusively from public training histories; require disjoint equal-sized recent and older windows excluding the final event. Draw replacement IDs from training-observed items, excluding padding, the target, and prefix items; approximately match original training-frequency bins and reuse the replacement multiset across paired interventions. Report matching failures and eligible-user coverage. Keep sequence length, left padding, occupied positions, and final-event identity fixed. Read features at the greatest nonpadding index, never count-1. Preserve timestamp slots only if timestamps are actually exposed; otherwise make no elapsed-time claims. Use shared unique candidates across variants, user-level bootstrap intervals, identity controls, and random-window controls. Restore RNG states and module modes. These diagnostics use training-prefix targets and do not replace the pinned evaluator. Preserve all four dataset routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], seeds 0/42, and the 200-epoch/200-batch limits. Any subsequent training change must preserve one HSTU checkpoint per category and update the embedded predictor writer.
idea.pseudocode:
cache validated training prefixes with user IDs
save module modes and RNG states
set view.model to eval; enter inference_mode
for each eligible prefix x with training target y:
    last = greatest index where x != 0
    choose disjoint recent and older windows of size k, excluding last
    sample a shared replacement multiset with approximate training-frequency matching
    candidates = [y] + unique diagnostic negatives excluding prefix items
    variants = identity(x), replace_recent(x), replace_older(x), replace_random_window(x)
    for variant in variants:
        assert padding, occupied positions, and final event are preserved
        features = view.log2feats(variant)[last]
        scores = view.predict_score(features, candidates)
        record target rank and top-10 membership
aggregate paired effects; bootstrap user clusters, keeping prefixes and variants together
return metrics and explicit metric_definitions, coverage, exclusions, and null reasons
finally restore module modes and RNG states

originality.positive: Combines fixed-slot content controls, preserved final-event readout, and matched replacements within the supplied HSTU diagnostic workflow.
originality.negative: Replacement interventions and paired ranking diagnostics are established methods; this is a methodological refinement.

future_potential.positive: Provides an inexpensive way to screen history-dependence hypotheses before spending the shared GPU budget on retraining.
future_potential.negative: Synthetic replacements can create distribution shifts, and sensitivity alone cannot identify user intent or guarantee validation gains.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires no backbone changes and uses the existing family-specific feature and scoring interfaces.
code_difficulty.negative: Frequency matching, eligibility accounting, and correct clustered uncertainty need careful implementation.

related_work.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces HSTU with aggregated attention, multiplicative gating, and relative attention biases.
limitations: Does not establish that the supplied checkpoint exhibits stale-history dependence or validate the proposed replacement diagnostic.

related_work.title: Measuring Recency Bias
contributions: Studies excessive recency dependence, motivating balanced recent-versus-older sensitivity analysis.
limitations: Recency sensitivity does not by itself establish useful relevance or transfer directly to the supplied HSTU implementation.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can produce comparisons inconsistent with full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned RecHarness evaluator or interpreting full-catalog rankings as complete user preferences.

related_work.title: TREC Product Recommendation Task Definitions
contributions: Distinguishes substitutes and complements through functional relationships.
limitations: Functional relationships alone cannot establish compatibility, ownership, current intent, or satisfied needs.
